items.title: Balancing discretion and equality in the new judicial clerkship model
items.summary: Becoming a civil judge is not decided by an exam alone. It marks the point at which a person steps into an institution whose daily work touches people's liberty, dignity, property and rights. Precisely because so much rests on that role, the principles of equality and fairness cannot stop at the examination hall they must accompany a candidate through every stage that follows selection as well. In Bhumika Trust v. Union of India , the Supreme Court laid down a new path for recruiting and training Civil Judges (Junior Division) by a 2:1 majority. Recognising that considerable time had already passed since the 2025 judgment, the Court devised a transitional arrangement, applicable up to March 31, 2027, under which selected candidates are deemed to have already completed one year of Bar practice. From there, they will be brought in as trainee judicial officers, spending a year in training at the State Judicial Academy and a further year in a structured law clerkship - 6 months under a district judge or a member of the higher judicial services and 6 months under a sitting Judge of the High Court so that, taken together, these stages fulfil the 3-year practice requirement. The matter is being heard by a Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran . items.title: ‘Are You King of England?’ Madras HC questions TN Minister Marie Wilson’s absence
items.summary: The Madras High Court, on Friday, August 28, questioned Tamil Nadu Finance Minister N Marie Wilson’s continued absence before a Judicial Magistrate in Puducherry in connection with an assault case, stressing that a minister cannot claim exemption from court proceedings merely by virtue of holding office. Justice V Lakshminarayanan made the observations while hearing petitions filed by Wilson seeking relief in the criminal case pending before the Puducherry court. The case relates to allegations that Wilson and his father trespassed into the house of his sister-in-law and assaulted her and her husband. According to a LiveLaw report , the judge orally remarked that ministers are not above the law and recalled that former Prime Minister PV Narasimha Rao had appeared before a court while holding the highest executive office in the country. “When Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister of the country, he appeared in court. You're just a Minister, Finance Minister of the State. Let us not give an impression that a Minister is above the law,” the judge orally remarked. items.title: Kerala police officer suspended over social media post targeting Muslims
items.summary: A Grade Sub-Inspector attached to the Thodupuzha police station in Idukki was suspended on Friday, August 28, for sharing a social media post containing communal remarks targeting Muslims. The officer, K Vijesh, shared a post originally published by a Facebook page called Snehi's Politricks. The post was on a video that had recently gone viral on social media, purportedly showing a hijab-wearing young woman kicking an Onam pookkalam. The video was circulated with a claim that the incident had taken place in Ernakulam district. The post shared by Vijesh alleged that the pookkalam was initially believed to have been damaged by a dog, but that CCTV footage had revealed otherwise Idukki District Police chief A Naseem ordered Vijesh's suspension on August 28, following a special report submitted by the Thodupuzha Deputy Superintendent of Police. According to the order, Vijesh had shared both the post carrying the video and the accompanying remarks from his Facebook account. The District Police chief found that the content violated the conduct expected of a police officer and warranted departmental action. items.title: Andhra: 31-year-old pregnant woman dies after alleged botched abortion surgery
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A 31-year-old pregnant woman died in Andhra Pradesh on Thursday, August 27, following an alleged botched abortion procedure. The procedure was reportedly performed by unqualified medical staff on the instructions of a registered medical practitioner (RMP) in Yerragondapalem, Markapuram district. The victim, Shaik Mahabunni, was six months pregnant and was admitted to a private hospital on August 25 after experiencing abdominal pain. Her condition reportedly deteriorated during the procedure, and she died two days later. Following the incident, the Andhra Pradesh Medical Council announced an inquiry into the matter. In a statement issued on August 28, the Council said it would investigate the allegations through its anti-quackery committee. An FIR has also been registered at the Yerragondapalem police station based on a complaint by Mahabunni’s husband, Shaik Chinna Balaji. Balaji believes that his wife’s death was caused by an existing health condition and not by a botched procedure. The case has consequently been registered as an unnatural death.
